subject: Reproductive
vignette: A 22-year-old woman undergoes a vaginal biopsy for evaluation of a lesion. Histology shows a multilayered epithelium whose surface cells retain their nuclei, with no superficial keratin layer.
question: Which of the following best describes the normal epithelial lining of the vagina?
explanation_correct: The vagina is lined by nonkeratinized stratified squamous epithelium: multiple cell layers with nucleated surface cells and no surface keratin. The ectocervix has the same nonkeratinized stratified squamous lining, whereas the vulva is keratinized stratified squamous epithelium (skin).

explanation_incorrect.A: Keratinized stratified squamous epithelium lines the vulva, not the vagina or ectocervix, which are moist mucosal surfaces without surface keratin.
explanation_incorrect.B: Simple columnar epithelium lines the endocervical canal and the uterine body, not the vagina.
explanation_incorrect.C: Simple cuboidal epithelium covers the outer surface of the ovary as the germinal epithelium.
explanation_incorrect.E: Pseudostratified ciliated columnar epithelium lines much of the respiratory tract, not the female lower genital tract.

educationalObjective: The vagina and ectocervix are lined by nonkeratinized stratified squamous epithelium; the vulva is keratinized.

subject: Reproductive
vignette: A 34-year-old woman has a Pap test that samples cells from both the endocervical canal and the outer cervix. The pathologist notes two distinctly different epithelia meeting at a squamocolumnar junction.
question: Which of the following is the normal epithelial lining of the endocervical canal?
explanation_correct: The endocervix is lined by simple columnar epithelium, whereas the ectocervix is lined by nonkeratinized stratified squamous epithelium. These two linings meet at the squamocolumnar junction within the transformation zone. Sampling this junction is the purpose of the Pap test.

explanation_incorrect.B: Nonkeratinized stratified squamous epithelium lines the ectocervix and vagina, not the endocervical canal.
explanation_incorrect.C: Keratinized stratified squamous epithelium is found on the vulva, not in the endocervix.
explanation_incorrect.D: Transitional epithelium (urothelium) lines the bladder and ureters, not the cervix.
explanation_incorrect.E: Ciliated simple columnar epithelium lines the fallopian tubes and respiratory tract, not the endocervix.

educationalObjective: Endocervix is simple columnar; ectocervix is nonkeratinized stratified squamous; they meet at the squamocolumnar junction.

subject: Reproductive
vignette: A medical student reviews a table of female reproductive epithelial histology and is quizzed on which structure is lined by which epithelium.
question: Which of the following structure–epithelium pairs is correct?

options.text: Fallopian tube - nonkeratinized stratified squamous epithelium
Ovary outer surface - simple cuboidal epithelium

explanation_correct: The outer surface of the ovary is covered by simple cuboidal epithelium known as the germinal epithelium. The fallopian tube is instead lined by ciliated simple columnar epithelium, and the uterine body by simple columnar epithelium with long tubular glands in the proliferative phase and coiled glands in the secretory phase.

explanation_incorrect.A: The fallopian tube is lined by ciliated simple columnar epithelium, which helps move the oocyte, not by nonkeratinized stratified squamous epithelium.
explanation_incorrect.B: The uterine body is lined by simple columnar epithelium with tubular or coiled endometrial glands, not transitional epithelium.
explanation_incorrect.D: The vulva is lined by keratinized stratified squamous epithelium because it is skin, not by simple columnar epithelium.
explanation_incorrect.E: The vagina is lined by nonkeratinized stratified squamous epithelium; keratinized stratified squamous is the vulva.

educationalObjective: The ovary's outer surface is simple cuboidal germinal epithelium; tube is ciliated simple columnar and uterine body is simple columnar with glands.

subject: Reproductive
vignette: A 29-year-old woman has a Pap test that samples the region where the squamous epithelium of the ectocervix meets the columnar epithelium of the endocervix. The cytologist notes that this junctional region is the most common site of cervical cancer and is the area targeted by cervical sampling.
question: Which of the following terms refers to this squamocolumnar junction sampled by the Pap test?
explanation_correct: The transformation zone is the squamocolumnar junction where nonkeratinized stratified squamous epithelium of the ectocervix meets simple columnar epithelium of the endocervix. It is the most common site for cervical cancer and is the region sampled by the Pap test, because cervical dysplasia arises in this actively metaplastic zone.

explanation_incorrect.A: The ectocervix is the portio lined by nonkeratinized stratified squamous epithelium; it is one side of the junction, not the junctional zone itself.
explanation_incorrect.B: The endocervix is the canal lined by simple columnar epithelium; it is the other side of the junction, not the junctional zone itself.
explanation_incorrect.C: The ovarian germinal epithelium is simple cuboidal epithelium covering the ovary and is unrelated to the cervix.
explanation_incorrect.D: The uterine isthmus is the narrowed lower segment of the uterus between the body and cervix, not the cervical squamocolumnar junction.

educationalObjective: The transformation zone is the cervical squamocolumnar junction, the most common site of cervical cancer and the area sampled by Pap test.
